message.content: {"summary":"You have set out a clear, well-motivated single-satellite concept in the Introduction, with a sensible sun-synchronous inclination at 600 km and useful STK access analysis. The main gaps are in the technical reasoning: the launch-site argument needs revisiting for a retrograde orbit, the RAAN and manoeuvre statements need correcting, and the end-of-life and referencing need completing.","next_steps":["Revisit the launch-site justification in Mission Design – Launch. For a retrograde ~98° orbit the Earth-rotation benefit of an equatorial site is much smaller, so explain why Vega E is still preferable, including the plane-change cost from 5°N.","Correct and complete the Orbit section: state the local time of descending node, orbital period, swath width and ground sample distance, and explain your RAAN and epoch. Make the manoeuvre statements consistent with a satellite that has no thrusters.","Finish Mission Duration & EOL with a decay or lifetime estimate supporting the five-year life, show the STK results, and complete the drag-sail description with its size. Replace the Wikipedia source with authoritative references and check every in-text citation against the bibliography."],"criteria":{"C1":"Your Introduction clearly states the primary mission, the bleaching and fluid-lensing rationale, why one spacecraft suffices, and the likely users. To reach Accomplished, name the operator precisely rather than 'Australia ground facilities', justify or remove the speculative funding comment, and replace the URL-only bibliography with full literature references.","C2":"Your strongest evidence is the sun-synchronous inclination (about 97.8° at 600 km), the STK access analysis and the orbit screenshots. The launch reasoning and RAAN explanation are currently inverted or incorrect, and the manoeuvre claims contradict the no-thrust design. To reach Accomplished, support major requirements with calculations (period, swath, GSD, decay), correct these errors, and justify the Mount Pleasant downlink with frequency and data rate.","C3":"Your conclusion makes sensible points about constant illumination and launch-vehicle risk, but it is largely generic. It does not cite quantitative results such as contact durations, pass counts or EOL lifetime. To reach Accomplished, summarise the key numbers from your analysis, state what they show, and acknowledge the remaining limitations.","C4":"The report has a clear heading structure and an executive summary, and most figures are captioned. Citation consistency is the main weakness: in-text references run beyond the bibliography, one number is used for two sources, entries are garbled, and Wikipedia is cited. To reach Accomplished, fix every citation, label all tables and Image 3 consistently, and proofread for grammar and typos."}}
